title: bls12-381-fixed-g2-invert-g1: Frobenius-class parallel Pollard rho in GT, success target 0.39

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (design of public submission 3da91365-2d58-40e5-ac7d-415e3061f7d8: compute g=e(P0,Q); solve z=g^x by parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT with R=1024 twisted multipliers, a 4-Fp-multiplication canonical-conjugate key, partition and distinguished bits taken from the raw class key, deterministic class-consistent fruitless-cycle escape, a 40/theta stuck-walk restart, and a distinguished-report log whose capacity C_rep = M * R_w = 2^20 * 2^47 = 2^67 records (direct addressing, 80 bytes each) is a deterministic bound: the two-cycle and checkpoint-cycle checks run before the distinguished test and a report is stored only if it differs from this walk's last stored record (same 128-bit key and same two canonical exponents), so the exact duplicates a fruitless two-cycle return would append are never stored, and an exact duplicate a longer cycle leaves is dropped inside its equal-key run as the same record rather than recomputed (a class fixes the canonical element, not the exponent pair: a revisit of one class with different exponent pairs is the useful collision, solved as x = (A1-A2)/(B2-B1) mod r from two equal canonical elements with different pairs), and each walk slot keeps a cumulative report counter, carried across a stuck-walk restart, and is stopped at R_w = 2^47 reports, so no report-count probability statement enters the memory or processing bound; the log is matched offline by an in-place heapsort of the whole 80-byte record (128-bit key T, then the two canonical exponents) with at most 67 sift levels per record at 130 instructions per 10-word compare-and-swap level (8,710, budgeted 10,000), so identical records are adjacent and duplicate removal is exactly one adjacent 80-byte comparison per record (100 instructions); each maximal run of d records that share the 16-byte key T with distinct exponent pairs is the only place pairwise work occurs, and all d(d-1)/2 of its pairs are charged at most 200 instructions each against a hard pair budget P = 2^41, the match being aborted as a failure when the log's total pair count would exceed P (at most (2^67)^2/2 = 2^133 pairs of distinct records give about 2^5 expected false-key pairs, so P(abort) <= 2^5/2^41 = 2^-36 by Markov), and the first pair whose canonical elements are equal with different exponent pairs gives x = (A1-A2)/(B2-B1) mod r, a genuine repeat of one canonical element with different exponent pairs being charged as pairs like any other; output P=[x]P0 and verify e(P,Q)=z) succeeds with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^125.826 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000), including setup, pairings, table construction, walk starts, distinguished-point handling charged at its worst case (2^66.15 units of record work at the cap, plus the 2^34.4-unit pair term), cycle handling, detection delay, output and verification. Peak memory is below 2^73.4 bytes (a hard bound: the 2^67-record log at 80 bytes per record plus the multiplier table and walk states, with no hash table); preprocessing is at most 2^31 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound relies on the standard random-mapping heuristic for R-adding rho walks (with the Brent-Pollard R/(R-1) correction and 3% explicit step slack; model success 0.4081 at the step budget), the same heuristic also giving the fruitless-cycle rates derived in proof.md section 3.2 and the probability, far below 2^-300, that the per-walk report cap stops a healthy walk slot; it is supported by toy-field experiments that run the production partition and distinguished-point predicates, the production step order and append rule, and the production offline matcher; no production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: on real BLS12-381 GT elements, check the Frobenius formula, the 4-multiplication conjugate-key formula, distinctness of the 12 keys, that the two-subtraction sign-set minimum equals the twelve-way argmin and class key, consistency of the canonical representative, p^6 = inversion, ord_r(p)=12. Part B: run the complete Frobenius-class rho walk (kappa trick, twisted table, partition h = K mod R and distinguished test on the raw class key as in production, 2-cycle and checkpoint escapes, stuck-walk rule) in a field q near 2^20 with the same tower shape, in the production step order (both cycle checks before the distinguished test) and with the append rule (a report equal to the walk's last stored record, same truncated key and same two canonical exponents, is not stored) and with the slot's report counter carried across a stuck-walk restart; every trial runs to the fixed step budget 1.03 S0, so no trial stops at its first recovery. The collected report log is then matched offline as production does: sorted by the full 80-byte record (key, then both canonical exponents) so identical records are adjacent, duplicates dropped by one adjacent full-record comparison, every pair of the remaining distinct records of an equal-key run enumerated and charged against the toy's hard pair budget, the canonical element g^A z^B recomputed for each record a charged pair touches, the logarithm solved as x = (A1-A2)/(B2-B1) only from a pair of equal elements with different exponent pairs and accepted only when exponentiation verifies g^x = z; the pair count aborts the match when it exceeds the budget, and a pair-budget stress pass checks that the abort fires. Each row reports the first-collision fraction and the recovered-and-verified fraction separately, both with binomial standard errors, the log length against its cap, the per-walk report cap scaled from R_w = 2^47 and the slots it stopped, the pairs charged and the element recomputations against the toy pair budget, 2-cycle rates, long-cycle counts and the distinguished fraction; a stress pass with a tiny cap exercises the cap rule, and a second stress pass forces stuck-walk restarts to exercise the persistent per-slot report counter (the log length equals the sum of the slots' counters and stays under M x cap). Part A2: measure the low 70 bits of the class key on real GT elements. Part C: recompute the fruitless-cycle bound, the deterministic report-log capacity M R_w, the probability that a healthy walk slot reaches the cap, the memory bound, the worst-case report-handling charge (append 1,000, full-record heapsort 10,000, adjacent dedup 100 instructions per record), the hard pair budget P = 2^41 and the pair and recomputation charges it bounds, and the work ledger (per-step count 2,026, budget 2,250, step cost c = 1 + 2,250/20,000, log2 W, claim >= log2 W). Toy scale only; does not validate production costs or production key statistics.
